items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: The name 'Russell' is mentioned by the [INTERVIEWER] in a disjointed narrative about a boy with talent and a trombone, but the [INTERVIEWEE] does not respond to or acknowledge this mention, nor does he mention Russell in his own extensive storytelling.

ctx.x: Oh, boy, that's all green juice. Nobody knocked with these doors.

Somebody said, that boy's got talent, so he got him a- Oh, I had him a- Oh, he grew on a bit right fast, man. Yeah, the trombone was getting out of the street. Russell's taking all of his time. He's incriminating the statements over there. He's making notes. I'm missing it. He's just incredible. Wow. Right in there. I'm finished telling you, I'm finished telling you, that something and then, I had a boy, I had a boy, and then I had a boy, and then I had a boy, and then I had a boy.

I used to have fights, advertised fights. But only six men in a way, six men, you know? In Italian, in the foiniture wagon, it's an old-time foiniture wagon. Hell, when I got two, I had a 60-man there playing the parade, all, just to go and see the fight. I was playing the marailles, I didn't care. I was playing the parades here, when the time of the parades, the parades used to break up in the French opera, and I suppose you had 12 men in there. The Green, Yellow, Nunes, Bill Jaloti, and who else? I can't think…
